judge_reasoning: The model's plan requires simultaneously dealing at least 5 combat damage to Gideon (loyalty 5) and at least 3 combat damage to the opponent's life total (3), using 6 attackers of power 2 each (total 12 power), while Bruna (5/7 flying) remains as the opponent's sole blocker (only Vampire Cutthroat is unblockable via skulk). Mathematically, it is provably impossible to split these attackers between the two targets such that both thresholds survive an optimal single block by Bruna -- the opponent can always choose to block a creature on whichever side has insufficient buffer, leaving either Gideon alive (loyalty > 0) or the opponent's life above 0, either of which prevents the loss due to the Gideon emblem's shield. The model never removes Bruna as a blocker (e.g., via Stasis Snare, which is left completely unused despite having enough leftover mana), unlike the official solution, which avoids this issue by exiling Gideon directly via Ayli's ability after already reducing the opponent to 0 life, sidestepping combat math against a blocker entirely. Thus the model's solution fails against a reasonable/optimal blocking decision by the opponent.

1. Cast Angel of Invention (fabricate: create two Servo tokens). All other creatures you control get +1/+1.
2. Cast Declaration in Stone targeting a Renegade Rallier (exiling both).
3. Attack with Angel of Invention, Vampire Cutthroat, Indulgent Aristocrat, Sacred Cat, and both Servos.
4. After blockers, assign (at least) 5 combat damage to Gideon of the Trials and 3 combat damage to the opponent among the unblocked attackers.

Puzzle conventions:
Winning
Unless otherwise stated, you must win the puzzle by inflicting lethal damage to your opponent before the turn ends. This can be as late as during the cleanup step if necessary. Your solution must work for all possible outcomes, such as your opponent’s actions and blocking decisions (see below.)
Phase
Unless otherwise stated, you begin each puzzle at the beginning of your first main phase. You have already drawn a card and gone past upkeep triggers. You have not yet played a land, cast any spells, activated any abilities of permanents on the battlefield, or attacked.
Your Opponent’s Resources / Actions
Unless otherwise stated, your opponent has no cards in hand and no other permanents in play (including no lands – despite the lack of realism there.) This means the only actions you need to consider are activated abilities with no mana cost. Most puzzles with opponent actions will offer more information on this.
Blocking
You cannot assume that your opponent will block a certain way, unless they are somehow forced to. Your solution must satisfy all possible blocking scenarios, even ones that would seem strange in a regular game, and always deal lethal in order to be correct.
Dice
Sometimes you will see six-sided dice placed on cards. These are meant to indicate counters, of whatever type is most reasonable to be there. On most creatures they will be +1/+1 counters, on most artifacts and lands they will be charge counters, and on most Planeswalkers they will be loyalty counters.
If the card specifies a type of counter itself, however (like Icatian Javelineers or Raging Ravine), that will dictate which type it is. 
For -1/-1 counters, we will use a separate graphic to avoid confusion.
Zones
Unless otherwise stated, all zones not displayed are empty. Neither you nor your opponent have cards in graveyards or in exile.
Cards Drawn from Libraries
In any puzzle in which either player might draw cards or otherwise access their library, the puzzle will stipulate some known or assumed information about the library.
Most commonly, this will be a statement that you should assume that the cards remaining in libraries are to be assumed to be irrelevant to the puzzle.
Your Life
Occasionally, your own life total might appear to matter – for cards like Anguished Unmaking, for example. If we require you to consider your own life total in a puzzle, it will be displayed.
If your life total is not shown, you may assume it is irrelevant and effectively infinite.

When you are ready to answer, put your final winning line inside <solution> tags:

<solution>
1. First step...
2. Second step...
</solution>

Your line must be legal under the rules and must win against all possible opponent responses and blocking decisions.

5459:704.4. Unlike triggered abilities, state-based actions pay no attention to what happens during the resolution of a spell or ability.
5460:Example: A player controls Maro, a creature with the ability “Maro’s power and toughness are each equal to the number of cards in your hand” and casts a spell whose effect is “Discard your hand, then draw seven cards.” Maro will temporarily have toughness 0 in the middle of the spell’s resolution but will be back up to toughness 7 when the spell finishes resolving. Thus Maro will survive when state-based actions are checked. In contrast, an ability that triggers when the player has no cards in hand goes on the stack after the spell resolves, because its trigger event happened during resolution.

5462:704.5. The state-based actions are as follows:
5463:
5464:704.5a If a player has 0 or less life, that player loses the game.
5465:
5466:704.5b If a player attempted to draw a card from a library with no cards in it since the last time state-based actions were checked, that player loses the game.
5467:

5469:

5471:

5473:
5474:704.5f If a creature has toughness 0 or less, it’s put into its owner’s graveyard. Regeneration can’t replace this event.
5475:
5476:704.5g If a creature has toughness greater than 0, it has damage marked on it, and the total damage marked on it is greater than or equal to its toughness, that creature has been dealt lethal damage and is destroyed. Regeneration can replace this event.
5477:
5478:704.5h If a creature has toughness greater than 0, and it’s been dealt damage by a source with deathtouch since the last time state-based actions were checked, that creature is destroyed. Regeneration can replace this event.

5480:704.5i If a planeswalker has loyalty 0, it’s put into its owner’s graveyard.
5481:
5482:704.5j If two or more legendary permanents with the same name are controlled by the same player, that player chooses one of them, and the rest are put into their owners’ graveyards. This is called the “legend rule.”
5483:
5484:704.5k If two or more permanents have the supertype world, all except the one that has had the world supertype for the shortest amount of time are put into their owners’ graveyards. In the event of a tie for the shortest amount of time, all are put into their owners’ graveyards. This is called the “world rule.”

5486:704.5m If an Aura is attached to an illegal object or player, or is not attached to an object or player, that Aura is put into its owner’s graveyard.
5487:
5488:704.5n If an Equipment or Fortification is attached to an illegal permanent or to a player, it becomes unattached from that permanent or player. It remains on the battlefield.
5489:
5490:704.5p If a battle or creature is attached to an object or player, it becomes unattached and remains on the battlefield. 5515:
